short_description: Tiny non-enveloped icosahedral +ssRNA virus (~30 nm) of the Picornaviridae (genus Enterovirus, species Rhinovirus A/B/C) whose ~170 genotypes cause most common colds; it replicates best at the cool 33-35 °C of the nasal lining and docks onto ICAM-1 through a canyon-shaped groove in its capsid.

colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; all colour here is teaching convention (see reference/colors.md). The cryo-EM reference is radially false-coloured.

labels.en: VPg protein (5' end of the RNA)

do_not_draw: lipid envelope or membrane bilayer (rhinovirus is naked)
surface spikes, corona of clubs, HA/NA-style projections, fuzzy fringe
perfectly smooth golf ball or a plain geometric d20 die
segmented genome or several separate RNA pieces
packaged RNA polymerase, matrix layer, helical nucleocapsid, nucleoprotein beads on the RNA
nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria or any cell organelle
bacteriophage tail, base plate or legs
a face, eyes or anthropomorphism; any text, letters, numbers, scale bars, watermarks

reference.note: No properly-licensed conventional TEM/SEM plate of a rhinovirus virion could be found (CDC PHIL, NIAID Flickr and Wikimedia Commons all lack one; Commons only carries X-ray-derived renderings). This EMDB entry image is a genuine cryo-electron-microscopy reconstruction of a native HRV14 particle at 2.9 Å-class resolution and is used instead, with modality declared honestly as cryo-EM.
